questions.q: A small particle moves to position $5\overset{^}{i} - 2\overset{^}{j} + \overset{^}{k}$ from its initial position $2\overset{^}{i} + 3\overset{^}{j} - 4\overset{^}{k}$ under the action of force $5\overset{^}{i} + 2\overset{^}{j} + 7\overset{^}{k}N$. The value of work done will be ______~$J$.
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
Work done by a constant force is given by& $W = Force \left(\overset{→}{F}\right) \cdot$Displacement\left(\overset{→}{r}\right), where,~$\overset{→}{r} = \overset{→}{r}2 - \overset{→}{r}1$

Given here,~$\overset{→}{r1} = 5\overset{^}{i} - 2\overset{^}{j} + \overset{^}{k}$~and~$\overset{→}{r}2 = 2\overset{^}{i} + 3\overset{^}{j} - 4\overset{^}{k}$

So,~$W = \overset{→}{F} $\cdot \left(\overset{→}{r}$2 - \overset{→}{r}1\right)$

$= ( 5\overset{^}{i} + 2\overset{^}{j} + 7\overset{^}{k} ) $\cdot \left[($5\overset{^}{i} - 2\overset{^}{j} + \overset{^}{k} ) - ( 2\overset{^}{i} + 3\overset{^}{j} - 4\overset{^}{k} )\right]$

$⇒ W = 40J

$

questions.q: A body of mass $2$ kg is initially at rest. It starts moving unidirectionally under the influence of a source of constant power $P$. Its displacement in $4s$~is~$\dfrac{1}{3}{α}^{2}\sqrt{P}m$.~The value of $\alpha$ will be ______.
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
Energy provided will be used to increase kinetic energy of the body. Therefore,

$\dfrac{1}{2}mV^{2} = Pt$

$V = \sqrt{\dfrac{2Pt}{m}}$

$⇒ \dfrac{dx}{dt} = \sqrt{\dfrac{2Pt}{m}} ⇒ {∫}_{0}^{x}dx = \sqrt{\dfrac{2P}{m}}{∫}_{0}^{4}t\dfrac{1}{2}dt$

$⇒ x = \sqrt{\dfrac{2P}{m}}\dfrac{2}{3}{t\dfrac{3}{2}}_{0}^{4}$

$⇒ x = \dfrac{16\sqrt{P}}{3} = \dfrac{1}{3} \times 16\sqrt{P}$

Hence, required value of~$\alpha = 4$.

questions.q:
A rolling wheel of $12$ kg is on an inclined plane at position $P$ and connected to a mass of $3$ kg through a string of fixed length and pulley as shown in figure.
Consider $PR$ as friction free surface.
The velocity of centre of mass of the wheel when it reaches at the bottom $Q$ of the inclined plane $PQ$ will be $\dfrac{1}{2}\sqrt{xgh}ms^{- 1}$. The value of $x$& (rounded off to the nearest integer) is _____.
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
If we take the wheel as a ring then its moment of inertia will be,& $I = Mr^{2}$.

Using mechanical energy conservation,

$Mgh - mgh = \dfrac{1}{2}mv^{2} + \dfrac{1}{2}Mv^{2} + \dfrac{1}{2}I{ω}^{2} ⇒ 12gh - 3gh = \dfrac{1}{2}3v^{2} + \dfrac{1}{2}12v^{2} + \dfrac{1}{2}12r^{2}\dfrac{v2}{r2}$

$⇒ 9gh = \dfrac{15v^{2} + 12v^{2}}{2}$

$⇒ v = \sqrt{\dfrac{2}{3}gh} = \dfrac{1}{2}\sqrt{\dfrac{8}{3}gh}$

Therefore,~$x = \dfrac{8}{3} ≃ 3$

questions.q:
If the maximum load carried by an elevator is $1400kg( 600kg\text{-Passengers} + 800kg\text{-elevator} )$ , which is moving up with a uniform speed of $3ms^{- 1}$ and the frictional force acting on it is $2000N$, then the maximum power used by the motor is _____________kW . \left(g = 10ms^{- 2}\right)$

$
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
The maximum force acting is,& ${F}_\max = \left(14000 + 2000\right)N$

$= 16000N$

The formula for power is given by,~$P = {F}_\maxv$.

It is given,~$v = 3ms^{- 1}$.

$⇒ P = 16000N \times 3ms^{- 1} = 48000W = 48kW$

$⇒ W = 48kW$

questions.q: A solid circular disc of mass $50$ kg rolls along a horizontal floor so that its center of mass has a speed of $0 . 4ms^{- 1}$. The absolute value of work done on the disc to stop it is ______ $J$.
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
Using work-energy theorem, we get

$W = ∆ KE$

$⇒ W = 0 - \left(\dfrac{1}{2}mv^{2} + \dfrac{1}{2}I{ω}^{2}\right)$

$⇒ W = 0 - \dfrac{1}{2}mv^{2} \left($1 + \dfrac{K2}{R2}\right)$

$= - \dfrac{1}{2} \times50 \times0 . ${4}^{2}\left($1 + \dfrac{1}{2}\right) = -6J$

Absolute work $= + 6J$

Therefore, required value of $W = 6J$

$

questions.q: A force $F = ( 5 + 3y^{2} )$ acts on a particle in the $y$-direction, where $F$ is newton and $y$ is in meter. The work done by the force during a displacement from $y = 2m$ to $y = 5m$ is ______ $J$.
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
If an object is moved by certain distance by the application of an external force along the direction of the force, then the force is said to perform some work.

Given, the force exerted on the object is

$F = 5 + 3y^{2}$

The formula to calculate the work done~ \left(W\right)$~by the force in moving the object from a position~${y}_{1}$~to another position~${y}_{2}$~can be written as

$W = {∫}_{y1}^{y2}Fdy . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . ( 1 )$

Substitute the values into equation (1) and solve to calculate the required work done by the force.

$\begin{cases}W & = & {∫}_{2}^{5}\left(5 + 3y^{2}\right)dy \\ = & {5y + \dfrac{3y^{3}}{3}}_{2}^{5} \\ = & 132\end{cases}$

$

questions.q: A body of mass $1$ kg~begins to move under the action of a time dependent force $\overset{→}{F} = \left(t\overset{^}{i} + 3t^{2}\overset{^}{j}\right)N$,~where $\overset{^}{i}$~and~$\overset{^}{j}$~are the unit vectors along $x$ and $y$~axis. The power developed by above force, at the time $t = 2s$,~will be _______W.&
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
Given,& $\overset{→}{F} = \left(t\overset{^}{i} + 3t^{2}\overset{^}{j}\right)N$~and~$m = 1kg$

Now, we can write from Newton's second law,~$\overset{→}{F} = m\overset{→}{a} = m\dfrac{d \overset{→}{v}}{d t}$

Then,~$d \overset{→}{v} = \left(t\overset{^}{i} + 3t^{2}\overset{^}{j}\right) d t$

Integrating the above,~

${∫}_{0}^{v} d \overset{→}{v} = {∫}_{0}^{t}\left(t\overset{^}{i} + 3t^{2}\overset{^}{j}\right) d t ⇒ \overset{→}{v} = \dfrac{t2}{2}\overset{^}{i} + t^{3}\overset{^}{j}$

Now, power developed by the force is~$P = \overset{→}{F} \cdot \overset{→}{v} = \left(t\overset{^}{i} + 3t^{2}\overset{^}{j}\right) \cdot \left(\dfrac{t2}{2}\overset{^}{i} +t^{3}\overset{^}{j}\right)$

=\left(\dfrac{t3}{2} +$3t^{5})$

At~$t = 2s$, power is~$P = \left(\dfrac{23}{2} ++3\left(2\right)5) = 4 + \left(3 \times32\right) = 100W

$

questions.q: A particle \left(m = 1kg\right)$ slides down a frictionless track \left(AOC\right)$ starting from rest at a point $A$ (height $2m$ ). After reaching $C,$ the particle continues to move freely in air as a projectile. When it reaching its highest point $P$ (height $1m$ ), the kinetic energy of the particle (in $J$ ) is: (Figure drawn is schematic and not to scale; take $g = 10ms^{- 2}$ ) ______________.
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
$K{E}_{P} - {KE}_{A} = P{E}_{P} - P{E}_{A} = mg{h}_{P} - mg{h}_{A}$
$= 1 \times 10 \times 2 - 1 \times 10 \times 1 = 10J$

questions.q: A block of mass '$m$' (as shown in figure) moving with kinetic energy $E$ compresses a spring through a distance $25$ cm when, its speed is halved. The value of spring constant of used spring will be $nENm^{- 1}$ for n =_____.
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
Using work $-$ energy theorem

${W}_{net} = ∆ KE$

${W}_{net} = \left({K}_{f} - {K}_{i}\right)$

$⇒ - $\dfrac{1}{2}$Kx^{2} = $\d$dfrac{1}{2}m \left(\dfrac{v}{2}\right)$2 - $\dfrac{1}{2}$mv^{2} ⇒ - $\dfrac{1}{2}$Kx^{2} = $\dfrac{E}{4} -$E$

$⇒ $\dfrac{1}{2}$Kx^{2} = $\dfrac{3E}{4}$⇒ K = $\dfrac{3E}{2x^{2}}

$⇒ K = $\dfrac{3E}{2 \times \left(\dfrac{1}{4}\right)2} =$24ENm^{- 1}$

Thus, the value of~$n = 24$.

$

questions.q: A $0 . 4kg$ mass takes $8s$ to reach ground when dropped from a certain height $P$~above surface of earth. The loss of potential energy in the last second of fall is ______~$J$. [Take~$g = 10ms^{- 2}$]
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
Displacement in $n^{th}$~second is given by~${S}_{n} = u + \dfrac{a}{2} \left(2n - 1\right)$

Here, displacement is 8th second is

${S}_{8} = 0 + $\dfrac{1}{2} \times$10 \times (2 \times8 - 1 )$

$⇒ {S}_{8} = 75m$

Loss of potential energy is~

$\Delta U = mg{S}_{8} = 0 . 4 \times10 \times75$

$⇒ \Delta U = 300J.

$

questions.q: A small block starts slipping down from a point& $B$~on an inclined plane~$AB$, which is making an angle~$\theta$~with the horizontal section~$BC$~is smooth and the remaining section~$CA$~is rough with a coefficient of friction~$\mu$. It is found that the block comes to rest as it reaches the bottom (point A) of the inclined plane. If~$BC = 2AC$, the coefficient of friction is given by~$\mu = ktan \theta$. The value of~$k$& is .......
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
Let& $AC = ℓ ∴ BC = 2ℓ ∴ AB = 3ℓ$

Apply work − Energy theorem

${W}_{t} + {W}_{mg} = \Delta KE$

$mg ( 3ℓ ) sin\theta - \mu mg cos\theta ( ℓ ) = 0 + 0$

$\mu mgcos\thetaℓ = 3mg / sin\theta$

$\mu = 3tan\theta = ktan\theta$

$k = 3$

questions.q: A ball of mass $4$ kg, moving with a velocity of $10\mathrm\mathrm\mathrm\mathrm\mathrm\mathrm\mathrm\mathrm\mathrm\mathrm\mathrm\mathrm{ms}^{-1}$, collides with a spring of length $8m$ and force constant $100Nm^{- 1}$. The length of the compressed spring is $xm$. The value of $x$,& to& the nearest integer, is ___ .
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
Let's say the compression in the spring by:$y$. So, by work-energy~theorem we have

$⇒ \dfrac{1}{2}mv^{2} = \dfrac{1}{2}ky^{2}⇒ y = \sqrt{\dfrac{m}{k}} \cdot v⇒ y = \sqrt{\dfrac{4}{100}} \times 10⇒ y = 2m$

$⇒$~Final length of spring,$= 8 - 2 = 6m$.

questions.q: The potential energy&  \left(U\right)$ of a diatomic molecule is a function dependent on $r$ (interatomic distance) as~$U = \dfrac{α}{r10} - \dfrac{β}{r5} - 3$~where, $\alpha$ and $\beta$ are positive constants. The equilibrium distance between two atoms will be~\left(\dfrac{2\alpha}{β}\right)\dfrac{a}{b},$~where~$a =______ .$
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
For equilibrium

$\dfrac{dU}{dr} = 0$

$\dfrac{- 10\alpha}{r11} + \dfrac{5\beta}{r6} = 0$

$\dfrac{5\beta}{r6} = \dfrac{10\alpha}{r11}$

$r^{5} = \dfrac{2\alpha}{β}$

$r^{5} = \dfrac{2\alpha}{β}$

$r = \left(\dfrac{2\alpha}{β}\right)\dfrac{1}{5}a = 1$

questions.q: A car accelerates from rest of $ums^{- 1}$. The energy spent in this process is $EJ$. The energy required to accelerate the car from $ums^{- 1}$~to $2ums^{- 1}$ is $nEJ$. The value of~$n$ is& _____.
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
The kinetic energy of a moving particle is given by

$E = \dfrac{1}{2}mu^{2} . . . ( 1 )$

When the final velocity of the particle becomes twice the initial velocity, the kinetic energy of the particle can be written as

$\begin{cases}nE & = & \dfrac{1}{2}m\left\{( 2u{)}^{2} - u^{2}\right\} \\ & = & \dfrac{1}{2}m\left(3u^{2}\right) . . . \left(2\right)\end{cases}$

Divide equation (2) by equation (1) and solve to calculate the value of~$n$.

$\begin{cases}\dfrac{nE}{E} & = & \dfrac{\dfrac{1}{2}m\left(3u^{2}\right)}{\dfrac{1}{2}mu^{2}} \\ & ⇒ & n = 3\end{cases}$

questions.q: A block is fastened to a horizontal spring. The block is pulled to a distance $x = 10cm$ from its equilibrium position (at $x = 0$) on a frictionless surface from rest. The energy of the block at $x = 5cm$ is $0 . 25J$. The spring constant of the spring is ______~$Nm^{- 1}$.
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
At first the block is pulled to a distance& ${x}_{0} = 10cm$(extreme position).

Potential energy of block is~${U}_{i} = \dfrac{1}{2}k{x}_{0}^{2}$~and kinetic energy~os block,~${K}_{i} = 0$.

Now, when the block is at distance~$5$ cm.

Potential energy is~${U}_{f} = \dfrac{1}{2}k\left(\dfrac{x0}{2}\right)2$~and kinetic energy is~${K}_{f} = 0 . 25J$

Total energy of block will be conserved, so~

$\dfrac{1}{2}k{x}_{0}^{2} + 0 = \dfrac{1}{2}k{x}_{0}^{2}4 + 0 . 25$

$⇒ \dfrac{1}{2}k{x}_{0}^{2}\dfrac{3}{4} = \dfrac{1}{4}$

$⇒ \dfrac{1}{2}k\dfrac{3}{100} = 1 ⇒ k = \dfrac{200}{3}Nm^{- 1}$

$= 67Nm^{- 1}$

questions.q:
A ball of mass $100g$ is dropped from a height $h = 10cm$ on a platform fixed at the top of a vertical spring (as shown in figure). The ball stays on the platform and the platform is depressed by a distance $\dfrac{h}{2}$. The spring constant is _____~$Nm^{- 1}$
(Use $g = 10{ms}^{- 2}$)
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
Loss in the gravitational potential energy of the ball= gain in the potential energy by the spring

$- ∆ P{E}_{gravitational} = ∆ P{E}_{spring}$

$mg\left(h + \dfrac{h}{2}\right) = \dfrac{1}{2}k\left(\dfrac{h}{2}\right)2⇒mg\dfrac{3h}{2} = \dfrac{kh^{2}}{8}$

$⇒ k = \dfrac{12mg}{h} = \dfrac{12 \times 0 . 1 \times 10}{0 . 1} = 120Nm^{- 1}$

questions.q: $A cricket ball of mass& $0 . 15kg$ is thrown vertically up by a bowling machine so that it rises to a maximum height of~$20m$ after leaving the machine. If the part pushing the ball applies a constant force~$F$ on the ball applies a constant force~$F$ on the ball and moves horizontally a distance of~$0 . 2m$ while launching the ball, the value of~$F ( inN )$ is  \left(g = 10ms^{- 2}\right)$
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
From work energy theorem& $F\left(0 . 2\right) - mg \left($20\right) = 0$

$F = mg\left($20\right)0 . 2$

$= mg\left(\dfrac{200}{2}\right)

$= 0 . 15 $\times$10 $\times \dfrac{200}{2}

$= 150 . 00N$

$

questions.q: A body of mass $5$ kg is moving with a momentum of $10kgms^{- 1}$. Now a force of $2N$ acts on the body in the direction of its motion for $5s$. The increase in the Kinetic energy of the body is _____~$J$.
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
The formula to calculate the change on momentum of the object is given by

${p}_{f} - {p}_{i} = ∫ Fdt . . . \left(1\right)$

Substitute the values of the known parameters into equation (1) and solve to calculate the final momentum of the object.

$\begin{cases}{p}_{f} -10kgms^{- 1} & = & 2N \times5s \\ & ⇒ & {p}_{f} = \left(10 + 10\right)kgms^{- 1} \\ & = & 20kgms^{- 1}\end{cases}$$

The formula to calculate increase in kinetic energy~ \left(∆ K\right)$~of the particle is given by

$∆ K = $\dfrac{1}{2m} \left({pf}^{2} - {pi}^{2}\right) . . . \left($2\right)$

Substitute the values of the known parameters into equation (2) to calculate the required increase in kinetic energy.

$\begin{cases}∆ K \text{ and } = \text{ and } \dfrac{1}{2 \times 5kg} \times \left({20}^{2} - {10}^{2}\right){kg}^{2}m^{2}s^{- 2} \\ \text{ and } = \text{ and } 30J\end{cases}$
